summary: Buildable alone in a month, cheap to run and services-first, so it fits the founder's constraints. But the buyer is a tax-office owner the founder has no network or domain standing with, selling is seasonal and one office at a time at ~$1.2k first-year value, and the compliance and liability side is a new domain. Viable if reached through a channel the founder's Windows/M365 credibility actually opens.

objections.objection: No route to the buyer. The founder has 'a few industry contacts' in security, not among tax preparers, bookkeepers or mortgage brokers. Tax owners buy security from tax-industry vendors they already trust (tax software, bank-product and hosting firms such as SBTPG with Watch Cloud and Verito bundle WISP and cyber services). A solo outsider has to win association speaking slots and owner trust from zero, and the 10-clients-in-a-quarter plan assumes a network that does not exist.

Time to meaningful revenue is long. Selling is limited to May-December, and today (late November 2026) about five weeks remain before tax season closes the window until May 2027. At $590 + $49/month, ten clients bring about $11.8k in the first year, not 'a modest founder income floor in the first quarter'. Reaching the ~$90k ARR target needs about 150 one-to-one founder sales, which is roughly two to three selling seasons.

The founder would have to learn a new domain. Their Windows/M365 skills cover the hardening checklist and the technical review. But the product's value claims rest on GLBA/Safeguards interpretation, 50 state breach-notification laws, reportability decisions and possibly acting as an outsourced Qualified Individual. Learning enough to be credible and safe would take about 2-3 months, plus paying for lawyer review of the decision tree. Note that 16 CFR 314.6 exempts firms with fewer than 5,000 consumers, which covers most 1-10 person offices, from the written risk assessment, written incident response plan and testing duties. A founder who doesn't know the rule well would oversell the very features being charged for.

Bootstrapped cash outlay before first revenue: lawyer review of the reportability tree and E&O/cyber liability insurance, which the concept itself requires, plus association sponsorship or conference fees to get in front of owners. These are modest for a funded company but real for a founder with no capital.

Service delivery scales linearly with the founder's hours. Onboarding, a yearly tabletop, incident support and reminders for 150 clients come to about 450+ hours a year on top of sales, and every hour of incident support lands at unpredictable moments. This is workable solo, but it caps growth unless a channel takes over delivery.

strongest_point: One-month MVP, near-zero running costs and paid-from-day-one productized service, with Windows/M365 hardening the founder can deliver credibly and quickly.
what_would_change_my_mind: Before May 2027 the founder lines up a channel that opens the buyer: one MSP serving 20+ accounting firms agrees to white-label or resell the program, or a state EA/tax-practitioner association books a webinar.
At least 3 signed annual agreements or 5 paid deposits come from offices outside the founder's existing contacts.
A lawyer-reviewed reportability tree and an E&O quote come in under $3k combined.

The concept is redesigned around a better fit: a fixed-fee 'M365/Windows Safeguards hardening plus a WISP that matches your setup' sold to MSPs that serve tax offices, with the incident clock added later.
